questions.question: When leaving your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Apply the air brakes.
Apply the parking brake.
Not apply brakes if the vehicle is left out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park. Place wheel chocks if needed.

questions.question: When checking the inside of a bus, you should:

options.text: Lock every emergency exit window.
Check every railing.
Remove loose handholds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check every railing.
questions.explanation: When checking a bus interior, make sure all railings and handholds are secure and safe to use.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, a bus driver should:

options.text: Stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track.
Drive slowly, but only stop if a train is coming.
Speed up to cross the tracks with momentum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track.
questions.explanation: Stop your bus 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track. Look both ways for trains before proceeding.

questions.question: To avoid hitting a hazard in the road:

options.text: You should always try to stop.
Swerving may be safer than stopping.
You should never swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may be safer than stopping.
questions.explanation: You can turn away from a hazard faster than you can stop. Swerving is sometimes the safer choice.

questions.question: Before driving, you should:

options.text: Skip the inspection report.
Only review the inspection report if passengers will be on the bus.
Review the previous inspection report if one exists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Review the previous inspection report if one exists.
questions.explanation: Start by reviewing the last vehicle inspection report. Only sign the new report if noted problems have been fixed.

questions.question: When checking your vehicle, you should look at everything except:

options.text: High tire air pressure.
Low tire air pressure.
Whether all tires are the same brand.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether all tires are the same brand.
questions.explanation: Check that tire air pressure is not too high or too low. Tire brands do not need to match.

questions.question: Before operating a bus, check that the:

options.text: Floor lining is easy to remove.
Handrails are loosely attached.
Emergency exits are clearly marked.

questions.correctAnswerText: Emergency exits are clearly marked.
questions.explanation: Make sure emergency exits are clearly marked and easy to access.

questions.question: Shaded areas of a road:

options.text: Usually do not freeze.
Have no moisture and cannot freeze.
Stay slick after ice melts on other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay slick after ice melts on other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sunlight and warm up slowly. They stay icy and slippery after ice melts elsewhere.

questions.question: If a vehicle's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working:

options.text: The vehicle will have no brakes.
The vehicle will still brake normally.
The vehicle will travel faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle will still brake normally.
questions.explanation: ABS helps prevent wheel lockup. If it fails, the basic brakes still work. Drive and brake as you normally would.

questions.question: When returning to traffic after a bus stop, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will let you merge.
Wait for a large enough gap to merge safely.
Have a passenger stop traffic so you can merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a large enough gap to merge safely.
questions.explanation: A bus needs a larger gap than a car to merge. Wait for a big enough opening before returning to traffic.

questions.question: Can you use radial and bias-ply tires together?

options.text: Yes, they should be used together.
Yes, they should be used together on the front.
No, they should not be used together.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, they should not be used together.
questions.explanation: Do not use radial and bias-ply tires together. All tires on a vehicle must be the same type and size.

questions.question: How often must you check that cargo is secure?

options.text: Every 10 miles.
Every 150 miles.
Every 500 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo security within the first 50 miles of your trip. Then check again every three hours or every 150 miles.

questions.question: What should you do with roof hatches on buses?

options.text: Remove them before driving.
Always keep them closed while driving.
You can lock them partially open.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can lock them partially open.
questions.explanation: You can lock roof hatches partially open for fresh air, but do not do this regularly. Opening hatches will slightly increase the bus's height.

questions.question: What should you do if there is a fire in your vehicle and you do not know how to put it out?

options.text: Use a fire extinguisher.
Try to spray the flames with water.
Move away and wait for firefighters.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move away and wait for firefighters.
questions.explanation: If you do not know how to put out a fire, do not try. Move away from the flames and wait for firefighters. This is especially important for hazardous materials fires.

questions.question: Which action is NOT recommended after an accident?

options.text: Try to move your vehicle to the side of the road.
Help injured people.
Drive away from the scene.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive away from the scene.
questions.explanation: After an accident, protect the area, call authorities, help the injured, collect information, and report the accident. Leaving the scene is illegal and you can lose your license.

questions.question: When are you most likely to encounter strong winds?

options.text: When coming out of tunnels.
When going into tunnels.
When driving on shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: When coming out of tunnels.
questions.explanation: Strong winds can push your vehicle out of its lane. This is especially likely when exiting a tunnel.

questions.question: What can water on a roadway cause?

options.text: Hydroplaning.
Speed increase.
Quick stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hydroplaning.
questions.explanation: Water on the road surface can cause hydroplaning.

questions.question: Why should you decide quickly what to do if your brakes fail going downhill?

options.text: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
The longer you wait, the more vehicles will move out of your way.
The longer you wait, the slower your vehicle will go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
questions.explanation: Act quickly if your brakes fail on a downhill slope. The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will move and the harder it will be to stop.

questions.question: What should you check in the fifth wheel gap during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: That there is a gap between the kingpin and locking jaws.
That the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
That the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: Look into the fifth wheel gap and make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you in a large vehicle, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Reduce your speed gradually.
Increase your following distance.
Increase your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your speed.
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, increase your following distance and avoid quick moves. Do not speed up—this will only make them tailgate at a higher speed. Do not use your taillights or brake lights to signal the other driver.
